Subject: High-commitment compute credit request — SustainAI pilot

Anya / team — looping you in and requesting internal approval path.

Summary: SustainAI (prospect) is asking for a one-time compute credit + 25% off list for a 12-month pilot that explicitly drives model-heavy inference (estimated 6M tokens/month peak). They are committing to an annualized ARR that would be above our high-touch threshold but want the discount to be applied up-front as a credit against monthly usage. They also want SSO & VPC, but that is already in scope for Dedicated starter.

Why this is exceptional:
- They are offering a 3-year platform commitment if pilot KPIs are met (we expect conversion probability ~55%).
- Their expected token consumption concentrated in first 6 months increases our unit cost exposure.
- Legal has pushed back on our standard auto-scaling surcharge language; they want fixed monthly caps.

Ask: Can we approve a temporary compute credit pool of $220k applied as monthly usage credits over the first 6 months + a 20% starter discount (instead of 25 requested)? This would be contingent on: 1) contract language limiting overage protection to the credit pool, 2) commit to 3-year term at renewal with step-up clauses, 3) prepayment of Q1 on signature.

Attachments: [Attachment: sustainai_pricing_memo.pdf (PDF, 412KB)] — includes usage profile, economics, and proposed contract language.

Notes: I included a simple revenue impact sheet and three alternative concession structures on pages 2–3. Asking Marissa & Karthik for exec clearance (VP/CFO) or guidance on modifications. If we approve, legal will need the redline (I can coordinate).

Thanks,
Dylan
Account Executive — Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

- Recommend limiting the upfront discount to 18% and offering an additional trial credit tied to clear KPI gates (e.g., 30k inference calls/day sustained for 30 days).

Karthik — can you flag items in the attached memo that would block CFO signoff and suggest a clean alternative structure? If you agree, I can route to VP for a quick note and then to CFO for formal signoff.

Marissa / Dylan — I reviewed the economics and legal asks. Short answer: CFO is open to an exception if we put hard guardrails around the concession. Proposed finance-approved structure below.

Finance recommendation (conditional approval):
1) Credit pool: $200,000 applied over first 6 months (max monthly drawdown = $40,000). Any usage beyond the pool is billed at published overage rates.
2) Discount: cap at 18% off list on the platform fee component only (not on usage overage).
3) Revenue recognition: Q1 prepayment required (minimum 3 months) to offset cash exposure.
4) KPI gates & rollback: If monthly inference calls exceed the forecast by >35% for two consecutive months, we reserve right to pause credits and revert to standard rates after 30 days notice.
5) Legal redline: attach updated term sheet with explicit credit expiration and audit rights. [Attachment: redline_terms_v3.docx]

Rationale: The $200k pool limits downside while matching their ask close enough to keep the deal economics attractive. The monthly cap prevents front-loaded runaway usage. Prepayment gives CFO comfort on cash flow and revenue deferral mechanics.

If you approve, I will prepare a short memo for CFO signoff (one page) and include the HubSpot deal link and expected ARR profile. Otherwise propose we counter with a $150k pool + a 15% discount and stricter KPIs.

Karthik
Head of Finance — Revenue Operations
